parts.note: the player's title opens with the name of a low-voiced singer, so that singer comes first, before the rest of the word naming a woodwind player

explanation.walkthrough: The concert-order picture hides the trick: the low male singer, a BASS, appears at the front of the word for a player of the bassoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of a woodwind player whose job title literally begins with a singing voice.

definitions.meaning: an innocent is a guileless person
American slang for an attractive young woman

explanation.surface: A naive young woman in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A babe is a naive, inexperienced person, and in American slang an attractive young woman.

clue.text: Wretched chap admits misgiving, not having married

explanation.surface: A miserable man confesses a doubt, being single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' removes M from QUALM, leaving QUAL, which SID 'admits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid means filthy and miserable, close in sense to dismal and wretched.

clue.text: Design punishment as an instructive experience

a lesson can be a punishment meant to teach

explanation.surface: Planning a penalty as a teaching tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a practical example that teaches something vividly.

clue.text: Refinements — delightful when found on the links

parts.note: delightful means nice
links are connections, or ties

explanation.surface: Golfing pleasantries: delightful tees on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the links' suggests a golf course, where delightful tees would be NICE TEES, which sounds like the answer; the wordplay itself takes links as ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine details or subtleties of manners, polite refinements.

parts.note: pieces of eight were Spanish silver coins, so circulating ones are coin money as opposed to paper

explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in the form of coins, which is what pieces of eight were.

explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage beside the fruit, but it is the verb meaning departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a place is to depart from it, the verb sense here.

parts.note: odd means occasional, as in the odd visit
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A peculiar party that happens now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball person or thing is eccentric, weird.

clue.text: Utter deceit in the art of government

parts.note: to utter is to say or state
craft is cunning, deceit

explanation.surface: Politics as total deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the skill of managing public affairs, statesmanship.

parts.note: blue jokes are shocking, risqué ones
a spencer is a short close-fitting jacket, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: A sailor scandalises someone named Spencer.
explanation.walkthrough: Spencer looks like a person's name, but a spencer is a short jacket worn in the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluejacket is an old informal term for a sailor in the navy.

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: perfect means ideal

explanation.surface: A scheme that is nearly flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a scheme or proposal, a synonym of plan.

clue.text: Improvement to cover for soldiers at the front

parts.note: an advance is progress, an improvement
a guard is a protective cover

explanation.surface: An upgrade to the protection for frontline troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance guard is the body of troops going ahead of the main force.

clue.text: It's said to put obstacles in the way of an alliance

parts.words: put obstacles in the way of
parts.note: to obstruct something is to block it

explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations or parties joined for a common purpose, a kind of coalition.

clue.text: Pleased to have taken a drink

clue.text: The smallest towels can get misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced letters are put in the wrong positions, so the word towels is rearranged

explanation.surface: Tiny towels are the easiest to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: The least or smallest is the bottom-most, a synonym in the sense of least.

clue.text: He uses devious methods to catch fish in Welsh river

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A man fishes craftily in a river in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To wangle is to obtain by trickery, so one who does so is a schemer.

parts.note: contact means touch
someone off is not at work

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with someone while on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch off something is to set it going, to trigger or start it.

definitions.meaning: as in an ... chance, a remote one
the outer surface or look of a thing

clue.text: Turned back, for example, to catch at the wicket

clue.text: Charge to be paid by you and me

you and me together are us

definitions.meaning: the damage or cost something exacts
to ring a bell slowly and steadily
